meeting_header: Date: 2027-08-25 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Evelyn Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (NovaPay Head of ML), Marcus Green (NovaPay Platform Eng), Leah Kim (NovaPay SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Evelyn (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining the weekly sync, we'll keep to 45 minutes; Marco's going to drive the perf notes. quick recaps — last run on friday we saw about 6.2k tokens/sec on the test model with continous batching enabled but we saw P95 climb, so main goal is to tune batching + concurrency.
[00:18] Marco (SE): yep, hi all. so quick numbers - baseline (no batching) ~1.8k tokens/sec, with continuous batching w/window=50ms we hit ~6.2k tokens/sec, GPU util ~74%, KV cache hit ~62% (note: some transcribed as KV cash in logs), average latency 140ms but P95 was 540ms when concurrency > 8.
[00:38] Sofia (NovaPay): ok those numbers make sense; our primary metric is tail latency under production load, not just throughput — we can't let P95 exceed 500ms. also we care about 99th.
[00:54] Marco (SE): understood. tradeoff is typical: batching gives better throughput and GPU efficiency but increases queuing and tail. we tested autoscale with redwood-dedicated nodes; when concurrency hits 12 we saw autoscale react in ~120s so there was a brief tail spike.
[01:15] Marcus (NovaPay): question, is autoscale based on GPU util or queue length? we want to tune to avoid those spikes.
[01:24] Marco (SE): it's configurable — you can choose queue-length based policies or util-based. for this workload queue-length triggers worked better in our earlier benchmarks, since util can be noisy with short sequences.
[01:36] Evelyn (AE): quick note, we can also set a hard concurrency cap per route and do gradual spillover to a lower-cost model variant as fallback, that helps with graceful degradation.
[01:48] Leah (NovaPay): and data residency / VPC questions — we need the test to run inside our VPC to mimic routing; Marcus will open peering today.
[01:58] Marcus (NovaPay): yes I'll do that after the call.
[02:03] Marco (SE): back to tuning — suggestions from our side: reduce batching window to 30ms, set target concurrency to 12 then run a 12->16 ramp test. also enable prefix KV caching for hot prompts, that bumped effective throughput in other customer runs by ~15%.
[02:26] Sofia (NovaPay): prefix caching sounds good. is that automatic or we have to pre-warm?
[02:31] Marco (SE): we have automatic prefix caching but pre-warm gives better initial hit rates. we also noticed some model-tokenization mismatch that reduced hits — so small prompt normalization helps.
[02:45] Evelyn (AE): do we have the spreadsheet link here — the one with configs? I'll share it in chat after call: (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/spreadsheet).
[02:56] Marco (SE): deep-dive into today's run. timeline: 14:00-14:30 UTC we ran ramp 1: concurrency 4->8, batching 50ms; ramp 2 14:30-14:55 concurrency 8->12; after 8 we started seeing P95 widening. looking at traces the queueing build-up before batch emission is where tail arises.
[03:20] Sofia (NovaPay): can you explain the queueing effect — is it because batches wait for the window to fill?
[03:27] Marco (SE): yes. with a 50ms window a request can wait up to that plus processing time; under low QPS batches are smaller so latency is fine, under bursty QPS you get bigger batches but also queuing. continuous batching also tries to prioritize latency with early flush heuristics but it's not perfect.
[03:45] Marcus (NovaPay): in our production traffic we have many short messages (seq len < 64) and some long ones; how do you recommend mixing?
[03:53] Marco (SE): a couple options — route short vs long to separate pools, or use dynamic batch sizing with sequence-length awareness; Redwood runtime has kernel selection so we can pin different models/quantization to each pool. separating short sequences into low-latency pool keeps P95 down.
[04:12] Evelyn (AE): that sounds like a product discussion we'll schedule; interim step is to get overnight test with concurrency bumped to 16 and batching window to 30ms and see GPU util and tail. Marco, can you run that?
[04:23] Marco (SE): yes, I'll set up two runs: (A) concurrency target=12, window=30ms, (B) ramp to 16 with same window. I'll capture p50/p95/p99, GPU util, batch size distribution, KV hit rates, and trace spans.
[04:38] Sofia (NovaPay): what about queue timeouts and retry behavior, we don't want client retries amplifying queues.
[04:44] Marco (SE): good point — set client-side timeouts slightly below server queue limit; Redwood supports HTTP Retry-After and can return early with a backpressure response if queue full. also we can cap per-key concurrency to avoid thundering herds.
[05:00] Marcus (NovaPay): how does quantization affect throughput? we saw better throughput in your previous docs but worried about quality.
[05:07] Marco (SE): int8 quant with redwood optimize helped throughput 20-30% with minor quality delta for our evals; for NovaPay's customer-facing lanes we suggest canary quantization on a small percentage to validate.
[05:20] Evelyn (AE): action items recap — we'll share spreadsheet and configs, Marco will run overnight tests, NovaPay will provide VPC access. any blockers on compliance docs?
[05:29] Sofia (NovaPay): need SOC two and ISO docs. last time the doc titles were slightly different so if you can send updated artifacts that'd help.
[05:36] Evelyn (AE): yes we'll include SOC 2/ISO and a short note on audit logging and KMS integration.
[05:43] Marco (SE): also wanted to call out an observation — when we bumped concurrency aggressively without trimming batch window, we saw tail spikes caused by an interplay between kv-cache eviction and large batch kernel launches; recommend monitoring hot-prefixes and TTLs. some logs had 'KV cash' typo but that's just transcribed.
[06:03] Leah (NovaPay): ok will monitor. we can also provide a sample workload trace to tune caching.
[06:09] Marco (SE): perfect. final proposed test matrix: 30ms & concurrency 12; 30ms & concurrency 16 ramp; 20ms & concurrency 12 as a stretch. we'll compare throughput (rps), tokens/sec, GPU util, batch size distribution, P50/P95/P99.
[06:27] Sofia (NovaPay): timeline is fine. can we get initial results by Friday morning?
[06:31] Evelyn (AE): yes we'll aim to have the spreadsheet and initial overnight logs by Friday 2027-08-26 morning UTC.
[06:38] Marcus (NovaPay): I'll open the peering and post credentials to the shared folder.
[06:43] Evelyn (AE): great; I'll send a follow-up with links and the invite for the deep-dive next week. thanks everyone.
[06:49] Sofia (NovaPay): thanks all.
[06:51] call ended
